messages:
maya: Heads-up — I flipped per-channel calibration on the FP8 path this morning and we see a throughput regression in staged canary. Quick numbers: host A (old per-tensor): 980 toks/s, host B (per-channel): 860 toks/s. Latency P95 up ~15%. :eyes:

raj: Ugh. I bumped into something similar on a local run yesterday. Kernel selection fell back from fast-fused-gemm to generic-gemm for some attention heads. Suspect quant scale range skew. Do we have a repro command?

lin: KV cache metrics look odd in prometheus — cache_hit_rate drops from ~0.88 -> 0.63 around the same deploy window. Could be prefix alignment or different KV layout with per-channel scales. Snippet from logs: `kvcache: miss 0.37, lookups 1.2M, avg_latency_ms 0.42`

anita: Can someone paste the exact perf run? I can run a bisect over kernel variants + calibration mode. Need minimal command to reproduce.

maya: repro (canary image tag redwood/infer:canary-20240715):
```bash
perf run --model-arch llama2-70b --precision fp8 --calib-mode per_channel --batch 1 --seq 128 --threads 4 --warmup 200 --measure 1000 
# flamegraph -> /tmp/ff-1719801234.svg
```
Performance regression is consistent across seeds.

perf-bot: automated check: canary image redwood/infer:canary-20240715 shows -12.3% throughput vs baseline (redwood/infer:stable-20240601) on batch=1 seq=128 benchmark. Regression attributed to kernel fallback heuristics.

oliver: Which calibration set did you use? If the calib dataset has long-tail values or extreme activations, per-channel scales can blow up one axis and change kernel tiling benefits.

maya: We used `dialogue-200k-mix` (customer-like mix with many long prompts). Found a few examples where activations had extremely high variance (excerpts below):
> example id 34211: max_act 14.2, mean_act 0.04
> example id 117002: max_act 9.7, mean_act 0.02
These outliers seem to dominate per-channel scale.

raj: That tracks. Per-channel uses per-dim max/min or percentile; outliers will force narrow quant steps elsewhere. Quick local patch: enforce clip to 99.9th percentile before per-channel calc. Ran one layer test -> kernel stayed on fused-gemm and perf improved ~9% vs naive per-channel.

lin: Also worth checking KV cache memory layout: with per-channel scales we change quantized tensor sizes in bytes slightly and that can shift alignment so the fast kernel path misses alignment checks. Try env var `REDWOOD_FORCE_ALIGN=1` to force kernel alignment and see if selection changes.

anita: I'll run three experiments in parallel: 1) per-tensor baseline, 2) per-channel + 99.9pct clip, 3) per-channel + FORCE_ALIGN. Will record per-layer kernel selection map and kvcache hit/miss. ETA 2 hours.

maya: Thanks. If that reproduces, we should consider a graduation rule: prefer kernel-locality-preserving scale transforms (e.g., clipped per-channel) or a selector that penalizes kernel fallback cost.

perf-bot: note: creating perf ticket INF-9876 for tracking. Autosummary attached: `regression: per-channel calib -> kernel fallback -> kvcache miss rise -> throughput -12%`

oliver: Also try per-channel but compute scales with global-block stats (group channels into blocks of 8) — compromise between per-tensor stability and per-channel fidelity.

maya: Good idea. Add that as 4) block-per-channel (block_size=8).

raj: If experiments show block-per-channel good, we might bake a heuristic: use block-per-channel for layers where activation variance across heads > threshold, else per-tensor. Cheap to compute during calibration.

lin: FYI I found one failing layer where fused-kernel had an alignment guard: `if ((ptr & 0x3f) != 0) goto generic;` The scale change shifted buffer by 8 bytes. Small changes, big perf impact.

anita: Experiments queued. I'll dump kernel maps + flamegraphs and drop results here.

maya: Appreciate it. If we end up with a mitigation path, let's schedule a short patch to runtime kernel selector (and add a test harness that asserts kernel choice invariant across calibration modes where possible).

anita: done. initial results: (1) per-tensor baseline 980 toks/s, (2) per-channel raw 860 toks/s, (3) per-channel clipped 940 toks/s, (4) block-per-channel (8) 965 toks/s, (5) per-channel + FORCE_ALIGN 955 toks/s. Kernel maps: clipped and block preserve fused-gemm in critical layers. KV hit rate restored to ~0.86.

maya: Solid. I'll open INF-987 with suggested mitigation: default to block-per-channel (8) and add 99.9pct clipping during calibration; fall back to FORCE_ALIGN in emergency.

raj: Nice sleuthing team. Follow-up: add an integration test that runs small calibration corpus and asserts no kernel fallback for the top-10 L2-norm layers.

lin: I'll add that test to the perf-suite and include a debug flag to dump buffer pointers to catch alignment shifts.

maya: Thanks all — closing the loop once we ship patch. :rocket:
